decision: translate opcode 0x50e0 (mask 0xfff8) as VOTE.VTG, a no-op
why: 4 movie/UI vertex shaders failed with 'unknown instruction 50e2432111170000' and their draws were skipped; 0101 0000 1110 0xxx sits between VOTE (0x50d8) and FSWZADD (0x50f8) in the Maxwell table the translator already follows (MUFU 0x5080, PSET 0x5088, PSETP 0x5090, CSET 0x5098, CSETP 0x50a0, NOP 0x50b0), and yuzu and Ryujinx both decode it as VOTE.VTG and emit nothing; it has no Rd, so no register is left stale
result: verified: zero 'translate failed' lines in b6; the shaders translate (their EXIT.FCSM_TR is the next unit)

decision: EXIT honours its flow test: T exits, FCSM_TR (0x1c) never does, any other test fails the translation loudly
why: after VOTE.VTG translated, the opening movie still showed black even with LARECOMP_MOVIE_TEST_FILL=200; the movie quad's VS (7248d3e000) has 'EXIT.FCSM_TR' at pc 0xb0 right after the VOTE.VTG, and the translator ignored bits 0-4 and exited before writing gl_Position, so every vertex sat at the origin; yuzu evaluates FCSM_TR as false too
result: verified: the opening movie renders (Kirby on the grass at frame 2900), no 'EXIT with flow test' failures

decision: translate LEA (lo form: reg 0x5bd0, cbuf 0x4bd0, imm 0x36d0): d = b + (+/-a << scale); .X/.CC/predicate output fail loudly
why: after the movie skip (PLUS), ~60 fragment shaders of the 3D title scene failed with 'unknown instruction 36d7...'; 0011 011x 1101 0xxx is LEA lo imm in the Maxwell table (yuzu, Ryujinx agree: Ra at 8, imm20 at 20, scale 39-43, neg 45); the translator had no LEA at all
result: verified: zero FS translate failures in c5; the scene after the movie draws but shows white (next unit)

decision: svcWaitProcessWideKeyAtomic writes the condition-variable key before releasing the mutex, as the console kernel does
why: the game froze ~5 of 7 runs right after the title scene loaded: a thread dump showed the main thread waiting forever on a job worker's done event (nn::os::WaitEvent, key 72c915fbc8) while the worker idled on its start event; the SDK's InternalConditionVariableImplByHorizon::Signal/Broadcast (sdk 0x70043510c0) skip the svc when the key reads 0, and the kernel HLE released the mutex before setting the key, so a signaller taking the mutex in that gap saw no waiter; Atmosphere's KConditionVariable::Wait writes the key first
evidence: work/kfl/runs/c7.log (dump), work/kfl/runs/k3.log (no signal ever ran with 0 waiters), work/kfl/runs/m1-m4.log
result: verified: 4 of 4 runs reach t=78 s without a freeze (before: c2 c3 c6 c7 s1 froze at t=52-56)

decision: translate LDS/STS (shared memory) next to LDL/STL: same encoding with bit 51 set, a 32 KB shared uint array in compute shaders (shortcut: fixed size, not the program's own)
why: compute shader 7273b10000 failed with 'unknown instruction ef5c000000070110' (STS: 1110 1111 0101 1xxx; LDS is 0xef48) and was never dispatched
evidence: work/kfl/runs/c5.log (failure), work/kfl/runs/d3.log (no ef5c failure, 18 dispatches at the title load)
result: verified: that compute shader translates, compiles and runs; the title scene is still white, so it was not the cause of the white frame

decision: translate SUST.P (bound, or bindless through a register MOV/LDC-loaded from c[2] at 0x120+8k) to imageStore on a writeonly storage image at binding 32+slot; bind it from the image handle (texture pool index) in the Vulkan backend; NVN IMAGE-flag textures get storage usage
why: first wrong pass: the deferred lighting (pass_019) was all zero because it multiplies the scene by the froxel fog volume t13 (80x45x32 RGBA16F, out = lit*T + inscatter); the two compute shaders that fill that volume (inject 10x9x8, integrate 10x9x1) failed to translate on SUST and were skipped, so T stayed 0 and tone mapping turned the black HDR image white
evidence: work/kfl/runs/p3.sum (pass walk), work/kfl/build/survey_*.glsl (only SUST unknown), work/kfl/runs/u2/pass_019.png, work/kfl/runs/u4/fin_5000.png
result: VERIFIED: both computes translate and run; fin_3400 shows the beach with Kirby, fin_5000 the lit first stage with Kirby walking; colour grading still wrong (pink sand: next unit)

decision: read NVNpackagedTextureLayout's low byte as two nibbles: block height log2 (bits 0-3) and block depth log2 (bits 4-7, for 3D textures)
why: after SUST the scene came through but tone mapping banded it (pink and yellow sand, striped Kirby); the tone map samples two 16x16x16 RGBA8 grading LUTs whose packaged layout is 0x40, which the old 'low word <= 5' check ignored, so they were deswizzled 2 GOBs high instead of 1; lut.py on the raw LUT bytes scores every block height / depth: only bh 0 bd 4 is smooth with identity corners
evidence: work/kfl/lut.py, work/kfl/runs/v1.pk.txt (layouts 0..4 and 0x40), work/kfl/runs/u2/pass_037.png (banded), work/kfl/runs/k1/fin_3400.png, work/kfl/runs/k1/fin_5000.png
result: VERIFIED: the beach and the first stage are graded correctly (sand beige, Kirby pink, forest green)
